objects.name: Phishing aimed at children and their families: 188 look-alike names in six sets
objects.description: Between 27 October and 16 November 2026 NSS recorded 188 new web names built to take children's and teenagers' game accounts, and through those accounts their families' money, devices and social accounts. The largest single piece is one server that answered for 40 names written for Russian speakers: Roblox sign-in and "Robux" names, a Brawl Stars gem store, Roblox script sites, look-alikes of the VK social network, a voting lure and a shopping look-alike, most of them each on a DNS account of its own. Beside it sit a Fortnite "locker worth" checker server whose newest 39 names were almost all unlisted, Roblox link names bought in four bursts, staged Mobile Legends "support" names and Minecraft "creator" invitations. On 16 November 161 of the 188 were on no threat list NSS takes in. This paper gives every name, takes apart the anti-bot gate that keeps the Fortnite checker off blocklists, and sets out what parents, schools and platform teams can do. Updated 18 November 2026: a check of every name the Roblox link pattern allows found 71 more, registered at the same registrar as the first 14 between 2 September and 15 November, so that set is 85 names, not 14.
